Legal cards to play

Source: R/play.R
sk_legal_moves.Rd

Given a player's hand, the game type, and the card led (if any), returns the subset of the hand that may legally be played. Skat requires following the led effective suit if able; otherwise any card is legal. In suit and grand games every jack counts as a trump, so leading a jack demands a trump, and a hand holding only off-suit jacks is not void in trumps.

Usage

sk_legal_moves(hand, led, game_type, call = rlang::caller_env())

Arguments

hand

An sk_card object or character vector: the player's remaining cards.

led

A single card code (or sk_card) that was led, or NULL if this player leads the trick.

game_type

A single game-type string, one of sk_game_types().

call

The calling environment, used for error reporting.

Value

An sk_card object containing the legal subset of hand. Always an sk_card, including when the hand is empty.

See also

sk_effective_suit() for the suit a card must be followed under.

Other play functions: sk_count_points(), sk_trick_winner()

Examples

hand <- c("HA", "HK", "CJ", "DA")
# Holding hearts, the player must follow hearts.
sk_legal_moves(hand, led = "H7", game_type = "spades")
#> 2 Skat cards: ♥A ♥K
# Leading, anything goes.
sk_legal_moves(hand, led = NULL, game_type = "spades")
#> 4 Skat cards: ♣J · ♥A ♥K · ♦A
# Void in the led suit: anything goes again.
sk_legal_moves(c("CJ", "DA"), led = "H7", game_type = "spades")
#> 2 Skat cards: ♣J · ♦A
